correctness.rationale: The Lindley survival is exactly a linear polynomial times \(e^{-\xi x}\). Both the DUS map near one and the alpha-power map near one are differentiable with positive finite derivatives, so they preserve the exponential rate and only multiply the leading tail constant. The resulting survival and density asymptotics give hazard limit \(\xi\). The tail-integral identity then proves that positive exponential moments exist exactly for \(t<\xi\).

value.rationale: Tail flexibility is presented as a central practical advantage of the proposed lifetime model, including its claimed suitability for heavy-tailed datasets. The exact asymptotic result shows that the entire family remains exponentially light-tailed and that alpha cannot alter the MGF boundary or limiting hazard. This materially changes how the model should be interpreted for extreme-lifetime and reliability applications.
